name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (compute, networking, memory) with leveraged semis beta for extra torque, a modest single-name short to offset gross exposure, and cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.

positions.thesis: Core AI compute bottleneck, highest-quality capex-cycle exposure. Stock pulled back ~4.6% this week to $214.72 (still far inside the -20% stop) as it consolidates into the Aug 26 print, which multiple outlets flag as the real catalyst -- normal pre-earnings positioning, not a thesis break. Holding unchanged through the quiet period.

Best risk-adjusted AI-platform exposure in the book. $483.24, +0.43% today, steady; 'AI boom bigger than investors realize' coverage keeps the platform narrative fresh with no new negative catalyst. Holding core size unchanged.

Custom silicon/networking diversification remains structurally sound; stock is stabilizing off last week's -5.94% air-pocket ($368.45, +1.2% off the prior close) and TD Cowen reiterates 27% upside calling competition fears 'overblown.' Keeping the de-risked 10% rather than adding back until the Goldman/EU-antitrust overhangs actually clear.

MI-series share-gain thesis just got a fresh confirming catalyst: BMO upgraded to Strong-Buy and Seeking Alpha flags the 'AI infrastructure flywheel finally turning,' stacking on top of last week's Taalas acquisition/debt-raise/BofA top-pick call. Stock at $473.25 and still trending. Sizing up from 10% to 13% to reflect the confirmed, accelerating catalyst flow -- funded out of cash, not by cutting another long.

HBM/memory structurally-tight thesis holds; CEO framing memory as 'strategic infrastructure of the AI era,' stock roughly flat at $966.78 after last week's recovery, with Aug 26 also flagged as a catalyst date. Kept at the modest 6% given the ongoing YMTC/China NAND competitive overhang -- unchanged.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Core theses across NVDA/MSFT/MU are unchanged and holding into the Aug 26 print cluster, so those stay put. The one piece of genuinely new, catalyst-grade information this week is AMD's fresh BMO Strong-Buy upgrade plus continued 'AI infrastructure flywheel' analyst commentary layered on top of last week's Taalas/debt-raise/BofA news -- a confirming catalyst, not noise -- so resizing that single leg up from 10% to 13% out of cash rather than rebuilding the book. AVGO stays at the de-risked 10% since it's only partially recovered (TD Cowen sees upside but the Goldman/EU overhangs aren't resolved). No confirmed name-specific AI/semis breakdown emerged to fill the mandate's optional single-name short bucket this week, so the book stays long-only rather than forcing a short without a real thesis.
